I wrote a multi-tab CDP driver, scratchpad\jobs-multitab\cdp.mjs: one Edge, one shared profile, N tabs, real mouse events. I ran it against fake servers with --step 0.3 and fresh --data dirs on ports 7925 and 7926.

What I exercised and saw:
- **Two and three tabs (s1).** A runs 3 images while B queues 2. A lists B's job as "Next, another tab's job"; B shows "waiting for the job ahead"; idle C shows "busy in another tab" and catches up as images land. At the end all three galleries match the server: no missing ids, no duplicate records or cards.
- **Server killed mid-run (s2).** I killed the server with taskkill /F after 2 of 6 images and restarted it about 4.9 s later. The owning tab says "The server restarted, and this job ended with it after 2 of 6 images", and the idle tab gets the restart note. Both galleries come back correct with no duplicates.
- **Frozen background tabs (s3).** I froze tabs with Page.setWebLifecycleState while other tabs ran 3 jobs, including a frozen tab's own job, then thawed them. Both caught up within about 4.5 s with no missing ids, no extra ids and no duplicates. The frozen tab's own job finished correctly after the thaw.
- **Pause across tabs (s4).** Pausing A while B is queued gives B "waiting: job ahead paused" and A "1 job waits behind it". Reloading A while paused reattaches with Resume. After A's job ends, A picks up B's job as "Another tab's job".
- **Network blip (s5).** I tried the network-offline emulation on a running tab. It did not cut the already-open SSE stream, so a lost stream on a live server is not really covered; the restart in s2 is the lost-stream case I did cover.
- **Budgeted grid paused (s6).** See finding 1.
- **[fail] prompts (s7).** I ran 1-, 3- and 5-image plain jobs with [fail] in the prompt; see finding 3.
- **Layout under the pointer (s8).** I measured with getBoundingClientRect at 1400x900 and 2560x1305; see finding 2.

gap-load-lifecycle-failures.coverage:
What I read: main.py (ensure_loaded, _load_failure, _switch_model, _restore_preferences, unload_model, lifespan, Server.handle_exit, run), jobs.py (stop_all, wait_for_gate, shutdown, cancel, _run, _finish), the shutdown section of design-notes.md, the rules.md Jobs entries, web/status.js unloadModel, web/job-queue.js and web/job-stream.js (ticker), and tests/test_api_analysis_lifecycle.py.

Setup: ports 7965-7967 were already taken by other processes, so I used 7960-7963 from my other assigned range. All data went to fresh --data directories under scratchpad/gap-load. I needed a real Ctrl-C path, and the stock fake calls uvicorn.run, which never reaches main.Server.handle_exit. So I used a scratch copy of tools/fake_server.py (scratchpad/gap-load/fake_exit.py) that serves through main.Server with timeout_graceful_shutdown=30, the same as run(). It adds POST /api/scratch/exit, which calls server.handle_exit(SIGINT) from a thread. It also has env knobs for a cold, slow or gated backend at startup, used with LOCAL_DIFFUSION_PRELOAD=true. Model: FLUX.1-Krea-dev, --step 0.3. Browser runs used tools/browser.mjs, with script JSON generated from Python. Most runs were at 1400x900; the stale-Unload check also ran at 2560x1305.

Exercised:
(1) A 15-25 s load with this tab's job and another tab's job (sent by fetch) queued. Cancelling the other tab's job removes its row on the next status poll (3.0 s measured). Cancelling the own job says "Cancelled — the weights keep loading…" and the page moves on to watching the other tab's job. The load continues and that job finishes.
(2) A gated failure with three jobs queued: all three fail with the gated detail. The card names the click-through gate and links to huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-Krea-dev (target=_blank). Retry load works after clearing the knob. Switch & load to a gated target leaves the picker and status on the new id, settings.json saved with it, state error with detail_url. Generate there fails with the gated text. Unload from error gives unloaded. Switching back without load is clean.
(3) stuck_critic then Switch: the switch_error reads "Could not switch to Animagine XL 4.0 Opt: the prompt critic would not stop; FLUX.1 Krea [dev] is still selected." The revision is unchanged, settings.json is restored (removed, since none existed before), the old model still answers Generate, and a second attempt fails the same way. Clearing stuck_critic lets the switch go through and saves settings.

findings.title: If the remembered More seeds count times the picked batches is over max_grid_images, the dialog never opens, so the count cannot be lowered
findings.location: web/more-seeds.js:131-166 (openMoreSeeds asks before showModal, using the remembered MORE_SEEDS_KEY count); backend/api_more_seeds.py:57-65 (422 for the whole request)
findings.observed: The dialog opens only after the first preview answers, and that preview uses the last count queued. If batches × count is over 1024, the server answers 422 "2 batches × 600 is 1200 images; a press may queue 1024. Ask for fewer, or pick fewer batches." That text goes to the gallery line and the dialog stays closed. Pressing More seeds… again gives the same result. The count box that would let you 'ask for fewer' is inside the dialog that cannot open. The remembered count only changes after a successful queue, so the user can either pick fewer batches or clear site storage. A realistic case: queue 64 more of one big batch, then later pick 17 batches (17 × 64 = 1088).
findings.repro: Fake server (FLUX.1-Krea-dev, fresh --data) holding images from at least two runs. In the page: remember(MORE_SEEDS_KEY,'600'), turn Select on, pick one card from each of two runs, press More seeds…
findings.evidence: Browser log: 'open=false | gallery line=2 batches × 600 is 1200 images; a press may queue 1024. Ask for fewer, or pick fewer batches.' A second press also gave 'second press open=false'. Screenshot b10.png shows the message in the gallery line and no dialog.
findings.finder_recommendation: If the opening preview is refused for being over the cap, open the dialog anyway with that refusal in #more-seeds-error and the count box marked aria-invalid (moreSeedsHold already handles /^\d+ batch/). Another option is to clamp the remembered count on open to floor(max_grid_images / batches), but that needs the batch count first. At minimum, retry the opening preview at count 1 and say why the count was lowered.
findings.verifier_reason: Reproduced on my own FLUX.1-Krea-dev fake (port 8010, fresh --data). I ran remember(MORE_SEEDS_KEY,'600'), picked ids 5 and 3 (two batches) and clicked #btn-more-seeds twice. Both times the dialog stayed closed and the gallery line read '2 batches × 600 is 1200 images; a press may queue 1024. Ask for fewer, or pick fewer batches.' Traced the cause: openMoreSeeds (web/more-seeds.js:134) accepts any remembered count from 1 to sheetPage (1024), and the server's count field also allows up to max_grid_images, so a remembered 600 is valid by itself. The opening preview then fails at api_more_seeds.py:57-65 and the function returns before showModal. The count is only re-remembered after a successful queue (more-seeds.js:355), so the user stays stuck until they pick fewer batches. The comment at more-seeds.js:121 says a selection refused as a whole is reported in the gallery line on purpose. That reasoning fits a selection that is too large, but it does not cover a count the user cannot reach to change. Nothing in design-notes 'More seeds' or rules.md:3361ff covers this case.
findings.verifier_recommendation: In openMoreSeeds, if the opening preview fails with the over-cap 422 (the message matches /^\d+ batch/), open the dialog anyway: put the refusal in #more-seeds-error and set aria-invalid on the count box. moreSeedsHold and runMoreSeeds already handle that hold. A simpler fix is to retry the opening preview once at count 1 (or at floor(1024/batches), taking the batch count from the refusal text) and say why the count was lowered.

findings.title: A Swap tags press made before the 400 ms check finishes is dropped: "Checking the swaps…" flashes and disappears
findings.location: web/tag-swap.js:390-394 (queueSwap returns on any hold) and 376-388 (syncSwapQueue clears the press's message once the check lands)
findings.observed: Mass refine and More seeds wait for the check of what the dialog shows before acting on a press (runMoreSeeds/runRefineBatch loop on the check). Swap tags does not. queueSwap writes 'Checking the swaps…' into #swap-error and returns, and when the check lands a moment later syncSwapQueue erases that message. So typing Find and Replace and pressing Enter or Ctrl+Enter straight away queues nothing, leaves no message, and the dialog stays open with Queue live. The user has to notice and press again. Doing the same in More seeds (edit, then Enter) queues and closes the dialog.
findings.repro: Pick one card that has 'smile' in its prompt. Open Swap tags…, type 'smile' in Find, Tab, type 'grin', then press Enter at once.
findings.evidence: A MutationObserver on #swap-error recorded ["Checking the swaps…",""]. 1.5 s later: open=true, Queue read 'Queue 1 image', and no new image was in the gallery. The same sequence in More seeds (type 3, Enter) gave open=false and the job was queued.
findings.finder_recommendation: Give queueSwap the same wait-then-act loop that runMoreSeeds and runRefineBatch have: if the only hold is 'Checking the swaps…', clear the timer, run the check and then decide. This keeps the three dialogs' presses consistent.
findings.verifier_reason: Reproduced with real key events. I picked the 'a cat, smile' card, opened Swap tags…, typed 'smile', Tab, 'grin' and pressed Enter straight away. A MutationObserver on #swap-error recorded ["Checking the swaps…",""]. After 2 s the dialog was still open with Queue reading 'Queue 1 image' (aria-disabled=false), and GET /api/jobs returned []. Traced the cause: queueSwap (web/tag-swap.js:390-394) shows the hold and returns. syncSwapQueue (376-388) then clears the message once the check lands, because swapRefused is false. runMoreSeeds (more-seeds.js:330-334) loops on the check before deciding, and Mass refine does the same. rules.md:3219 does say 'a press saying it in #swap-error', but the message is wiped within about 400 ms, so in practice the press is silently dropped. The inconsistency with the other two dialogs stands.
findings.verifier_recommendation: Give queueSwap runMoreSeeds' loop: while swapAsking is set or JSON.stringify(swapPayload()) !== swapAnswerKey (and the payload has swaps), clearTimeout the timer and await the swap check, then bail if the dialog closed. After that, read swapHold() and either say the hold or queue. That needs the check function to return a promise, as runMoreSeedsCheck does.

findings.title: Opening the recycle bin silently throws away the whole gallery selection, up to 1024 picks

Nothing is shown in #gallery-error, the Bin title gives no warning, and there is no undo. findings.title: A stale *.png.part or *.webp.part in the images folder blocks every bundle export, import and even the counts, permanently. Nothing in the app sweeps it or explains how to fix it.
findings.observed: _inventory() refuses on any name ending in .part. preview(), export_bundle() and import_bundle() all call it. The only cleanup at startup and before each bundle operation is discard_bundle_leftovers. It filters _stale_partials() down to _bundle_leftovers() (bundles/*.part, .bundle-* work folders, staging), so image partials are never removed, however old. Only clear_history sweeps them, and that is the CLI that deletes the gallery. The dialog shows 'The gallery counts could not be read.', Bundle & clear is held with 'Refresh the gallery counts first', and the status line says 'finish or recover the incomplete image write first: 20261001-000000-5-abc.png.part'. It gives no folder and no action, and nothing in the UI can 'recover' anything. A power cut or a killed process during image.save leaves exactly this file (storage.py:524-581).
findings.repro:
1. Start fake_server --port 7915 --data <scratch>/data-1 and generate a few images.
2. Create outputs/20261001-000000-5-abc.png.part with an mtime a week old.
3. GET /api/gallery/bundles/preview.
4. POST /api/gallery/bundles/import with a saved bundle.
5. Restart the server and repeat step 3.
findings.evidence: preview returns 400 {"detail":"finish or recover the incomplete image write first: 20261001-000000-5-abc.png.part"}. The import status is state=failed with the same error. After a restart the file is still there and preview still refuses. Screenshot: scratchpad/storage-bin-bundles/b1-bundles-part.png.
findings.finder_recommendation: Sweep image partials older than PARTIAL_SETTLE_SECONDS at startup and before each bundle operation, under the reservation that is already held. Handle a stale partial whose final name a row already names, with the .png missing (a rename that failed after commit), separately: rename it into place rather than discard it. At minimum, ignore stale partials in _inventory and keep the refusal only for fresh ones. Have the message name the folder and say 'delete it, or wait an hour if a render is running'.
findings.verifier_reason: Reproduced on my own fake (port 8015, scratch data-1). I planted outputs/20261001-000000-5-abc.png.part with an mtime 7 days old. GET /api/gallery/bundles/preview returned 400 {"detail":"finish or recover the incomplete image write first: 20261001-000000-5-abc.png.part"}. After a full server restart the file was still there and preview still refused. Traced the cause: storage.discard_bundle_leftovers (storage.py:688-691) only removes paths that are both in _stale_partials() and in _bundle_leftovers(). Image partials (outputs/*.part, thumbnails/*.part) are in the first list but never the second. lifespan (main.py:233) and export_bundle/import_bundle (bundles.py:265, 390) call only that sweep. The one place that removes stale image partials is clear_history (gallery_delete.py:448). design-notes 'Atomic PNG writes' and the bundle section document the refusal for an in-flight .part, but the reason (a fresh partial may be an encode in progress) does not apply past PARTIAL_SETTLE_SECONDS, and nothing documents a permanent block. Not in earlier reviews: review-2026-09-07 #8f947a9 covered clear/summarise only.
findings.verifier_recommendation: Under the reservation the bundle operation already holds, sweep image and thumbnail partials older than PARTIAL_SETTLE_SECONDS at startup and before each bundle operation. A stale <name>.png.part whose final name a row already names, with the .png missing, is the only copy of a committed image (the rename failed after commit, see storage.py:576-581). Rename that one into place, never discard it. clear_history's sweep has the same blind spot and should get the same treatment. Keep _inventory's refusal for fresh partials only, and make the message name the folder and the action: 'outputs\X.png.part is an unfinished image write; if no render is running, delete it'.

findings.title: Empty recycle bin pins only the count, so a restore plus a bin in another tab lets it permanently delete an image the confirmation never covered
findings.observed: The confirmation is for N images and the server only checks COUNT(*) == expected. If another tab restores one image and bins a different one while the dialog is open, the count is unchanged. The delete then goes ahead and permanently removes the newly binned image. bin.js's comment says 'an image binned meanwhile - in another tab - refuses the whole delete', which does not hold in this case. The confirmation's sources_in_use list was also worked out for the old set.
findings.repro:
With images 14 and 15 in the bin:
1. GET /api/gallery/bin/summary (records 2).
2. POST /api/images/restore {ids:[14]}.
3. POST /api/images/bin {ids:[20]}.
4. DELETE /api/gallery/bin?expected=2.
findings.evidence: The response was {"deleted":[15,20],"files":2}. Image 20, binned after the summary was read, is gone from disk.
findings.finder_recommendation: Pin the set as well as its size. For example, the summary returns max(binned_at) or a digest of the binned ids, and the DELETE compares it under the write lock alongside expected.
findings.verifier_reason: Reproduced over HTTP on port 8015. I binned 5 and 6, and the summary reported records 2. I then restored 6, binned 4, and sent DELETE /api/gallery/bin?expected=2. The response was {"deleted":[4,5],"files":2}: image 4, binned after the summary was read, was permanently deleted. gallery_delete.empty_bin checks only COUNT(*) == expected. The count-only pin is documented in rules.md (Empty bin and Delete unstarred), but bin.js:303-305's own comment says 'an image binned meanwhile - in another tab - refuses the whole delete', and that does not hold when a restore in the same window offsets the count. Severity stays low: it needs two tabs, and the image deleted was one the user had chosen to discard.
findings.verifier_recommendation: Have /api/gallery/bin/summary return a pin on the set, either max(binned_at) together with max(id) or a short digest of the sorted binned ids. Send it back with the DELETE and compare it under the write lock beside expected, answering 409 'The bin changed; look again.' on a mismatch. An ids-scoped delete (see the Delete picked feature) would close this as well.

findings.title: A search with an integer above SQLite's 64-bit range returns a 500, and the page shows 'Internal Server Error'
findings.location: backend/search.py:120-128 (_cast), backend/api_gallery.py (list routes catch only ValueError)
findings.observed: _cast(int, …) accepts any length, and sqlite3 then raises OverflowError, which is not a ValueError. Every route that uses the grammar returns 500: /api/gallery, /api/gallery/bin and /api/gallery/unstarred. The clear and stats CLIs reach the same filter_clause. The gallery shows 0 cards and an empty count, and the gallery error line reads 'Internal Server Error'.
findings.repro: Type seed:99999999999999999999 into the search box and press Enter. Also id:…, steps:>=…, or the range seed:1-99999999999999999999.
findings.evidence: curl /api/gallery?search=seed:99999999999999999999 returns HTTP 500. The server log shows OverflowError: Python int too large to convert to SQLite INTEGER at storage._page (storage.py:935). browser.mjs log: galErr 'Internal Server Error', cards 0. Screenshot: b1-overflow.png.
findings.finder_recommendation: In _cast, refuse ints outside [-2**63, 2**63-1] with a ValueError such as 'seed: … is out of range', so it reaches the existing 422 path.
findings.verifier_reason: Reproduced on port 8015. GET /api/gallery?search= with seed:99999999999999999999, id:1-99999999999999999999 or steps:>=99999999999999999999 returned HTTP 500 each time, and /api/gallery/bin and /api/gallery/unstarred also returned 500. The server log shows 'OverflowError: Python int too large to convert to SQLite INTEGER'. search._cast (search.py:128-132) catches only a ValueError from int(), which accepts any size. Not in earlier reviews: the 2026-08-29 OverflowError item was about seed wrapping on save.
findings.verifier_recommendation: In _cast, after converting an int, raise ValueError(f"{key}: {raw!r} is out of range") when the value lies outside [-2**63, 2**63-1], so it takes the existing 422 path. Add a test in tests/test_search*.py.

findings.title: `lora:none` (and `quant:none`, `model:none`) does a substring match on the word 'none' instead of matching IS NULL, despite search.py's own comment
findings.observed: The FILTERS comment says '`lora:none` is everything rendered without one'. For text keys, filter_clause returns the LIKE clause before NULL_TOKENS is checked. So lora:none means LIKE '%none%' and finds nothing, and the images made without a LoRA cannot be found by search. The same applies to quant:none for unquantised rows. lightbox-cfg.js:108 even says 'there is no term for "no adapter"', which contradicts the backend comment.
findings.repro: In a gallery with no LoRA images, search lora:none, then quant:none, and compare with refine:none.
findings.evidence: lora:none returned 0. quant:none returned 0, although rows with quantization None exist. refine:none returned 9 of 9.
findings.finder_recommendation: For lora and quant, treat an exact none/null/off token as IS NULL ('=none' stays the literal value). Add lora:none to the search tip and to lightbox-cfg's terms. Or, if this is not wanted, fix the comment.
findings.verifier_reason: Real for lora, refuted for quant. Code trace: search.filter_clause returns the LIKE branch for str keys (search.py:108-117) before NULL_TOKENS is checked, so lora:none means LIKE '%none%'. On port 8015, lora:none returned total 0 while every row has lora null, contradicting search.py:36's comment. The quant:none part is wrong: an unquantised load stores the literal mode string 'none' (loader_choices.py:16, config QUANT_MODES), so quant:none's substring match does find BF16 renders. My fake's rows are fp8, which is why that search returned 0. NULL quantization occurs only on legacy or imported rows. model_id is never NULL. lightbox-cfg.js:108 already says there is no term for 'no adapter', so the bug is the comment versus the behaviour, and lora is the only key affected.
findings.verifier_recommendation: In filter_clause, treat an exact none/null/off on lora as 'lora IS NULL' (lora:=none stays the literal name). Leave quant alone, since 'none' is a real stored value there. Then build lora:none into lightbox-cfg's terms and the search tip. If this is not wanted, correct the comment at search.py:36 instead.

findings.title: A tracked PNG missing from disk blocks Bundle & clear, and the message names a filename the gallery cannot search for
findings.observed: If one row's PNG is gone (deleted by hand, or left by a failed delete), the preview refuses: 'the original image is missing: 20261012-102440-102-99a8c0.png; nothing was archived'. findings.evidence: preview returns 400 with the message above. A filename search returns total 0. GET /api/images/16 is still 200.

findings.title: Feature: Bundle export always clears the gallery; offer 'Save a backup' that keeps everything in place
findings.observed: The only export is 'Bundle & clear gallery'. A user who wants a password-protected, verified backup of the gallery (for example before a reinstall or a risky change) has to clear it and then re-import. That means two full copies and new ids, because the gallery's ids are renumbered on import. Everything up to _verify_archive and the rename is already a self-contained backup, and only the cleanup block clears.
findings.repro: Open Bundles…: the only action is 'Bundle & clear gallery', which requires typing the record count.
findings.evidence: export_bundle always runs the 'clearing' phase after verification. No parameter skips it.
findings.finder_recommendation: Add a `clear: bool` to ExportRequest. Without it, return after `partial.rename(final)`, with no typed count needed and deleted_ids empty. In the dialog, add a 'Save backup' button beside 'Bundle & clear'.
findings.verifier_reason: Checked that it does not exist. export_bundle (bundles.py) always moves on to the 'checking' and 'clearing' phases once partial.rename(final) is done and the result dict is built (around bundles.py:323-345). No parameter skips them, and the dialog offers only Bundle & clear. Neither design-notes nor earlier reviews declined a non-clearing export. It is feasible, with no GPU involved: the verified archive is complete before cleanup starts. Importing such a backup back into the same gallery is already idempotent, because filename uniqueness makes the rows 'present'.
findings.verifier_recommendation: Add `clear: bool = True` to the export request. When false, return right after the rename with cleared=false and deleted_ids=[], and skip the typed-count gate. That gate exists for the destructive path. Add a 'Save backup' button beside 'Bundle & clear gallery', and word the done message so 'not completely cleared' does not read as a warning (renderBundleResult currently treats !cleared as a failure). Update the bundle tests and smoke-bundles. Effort is M rather than S, because of the result wording and the smoke and rules updates.

findings.title: Feature: after an import, offer 'Show imported', because imported images get the newest ids and land above today's renders
findings.observed: Imported rows get ids above every local one, while their created_at stays old. The gallery and the 'newest' estimate samplers (gallery_reports ORDER BY id DESC) treat them as the most recent. In data-1, archived images 12-20 from earlier in the day are listed above the frog images 10-11 made after the clear. Nothing tells the user which images just arrived, and nothing filters for them.
findings.repro:
1. Export, then generate 2 images.
2. Import the bundle.
3. GET /api/gallery: ids 20…12 (older created_at) come before 11 and 10.
findings.finder_recommendation: Return first_id and last_id in the import result (they are contiguous), and add a 'Show imported' button that sets the search to id:<first>-<last>.
findings.verifier_reason: Traced: import assigns next_id += 1 per pending row under the reservation (bundles.py:453-493), so imported ids form one contiguous run above every local id. The gallery orders by id DESC, so imported (older) images sit above renders made after the export. Gallery id monotonicity is a documented rule, so the ordering is deliberate and only discoverability is missing. The result carries no id range.
findings.verifier_recommendation: Return first_id and last_id in the import result, and add a 'Show imported' link in #bundle-status that sets the search to id:<first>-<last> through showGallerySearch. Optionally add 'binned K' to the same line (see finding 2).

findings.title: Feature: in the bin, a 'Delete picked permanently' action and an optional age-based empty

findings.evidence: Screenshot b3-empty-confirm.png (2560x1305): 'Permanently delete all 3 images in the recycle bin… That is every one of them, not only those this search shows.'
findings.finder_recommendation: Add 'Delete picked permanently' (an ids-scoped DELETE with the same typed or confirmed count). Optionally add 'Empty items binned over 30 days ago', using binned_at, and show 'binned 3 days ago' on bin cards.
findings.verifier_reason: Checked web/bin.js and api_gallery.py. The only bin actions are Restore picked (bin.js:348), per-card Delete permanently (DELETE /api/images/{id}) and Empty bin (DELETE /api/gallery/bin?expected=N). No route deletes a set of ids permanently, and nothing shows or uses binned_at apart from the binned flag (bin.js:42). Feasible with no GPU or architecture concerns.

Add a 'Delete picked permanently' button beside Restore picked, aria-disabled with a reason when nothing is picked, behind the same askConfirm wording as Empty bin. findings.title: Bundle error messages from the worker are shown raw, in lowercase and without a full stop, unlike the password-check route
findings.observed: The saved-bundle Import button skips the up-front password check, so a wrong password reaches the dialog as 'the bundle password is incorrect'. The same goes for 'the bundle is damaged: File is not a zip file' and 'finish or recover the incomplete image write first: …'. The /password route capitalises and adds a full stop; the worker path does not.
findings.repro: Bundles… → type a wrong password → Import on a Protected saved bundle.
findings.evidence: browser.mjs log: #bundle-status = 'the bundle password is incorrect'.
findings.finder_recommendation: Capitalise the first letter and add a full stop in BundleManager.fail (or in renderBundleResult), as check_password already does.
findings.verifier_reason: Traced: the saved-bundle Import calls startBundleOperation without a `before` password check (only the upload path sets check, bundles.js:352). The worker's error is stored as str(exc) unchanged in BundleManager.fail (api_bundles.py:103-106) and shown as-is (bundles.js:201). bundle_crypto.py:99/203 raise 'the bundle password is incorrect' and bundle_archive.py:242 raises 'the bundle is damaged: …', both lowercase with no full stop, while the /password route capitalises and adds one (api_bundles.py:200).
findings.verifier_recommendation: Normalise in BundleManager.fail: capitalise the first letter and add a full stop when the text does not end in one, matching check_password. Keep the fallback message as it is.

findings.title: --menu keeps the saved 'Load automatically on startup' from a different checkpoint, so the menu's new pick auto-loads with the old model's settings, and the page then claims those saved options were set aside
findings.location: backend/launch.py:281-291 (configure: apply_saved_environment runs before the menu; overrides for --menu omit load_on_startup); backend/startup_preferences.py:171-194; web/model-switch.js:488-500
findings.observed: Saved settings were Anima, BF16, no offload, load_on_startup=true. I ran configure(['--menu']), pressed Enter at Quantization (the saved BF16 was the marked default), chose 1 (FLUX.1 Krea [dev]) and pressed Enter at Offload (saved 'none' marked). The resulting environment was LOCAL_DIFFUSION_MODEL_ID=black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-Krea-dev, QUANT=none, OFFLOAD=none, PRELOAD=true, STARTUP_OVERRIDES={"model_id":"--menu","quantization":"--menu","offload":"--menu"}. So FLUX Krea dev in BF16 with no offload starts loading at launch. That is the case apply_saved_environment's docstring says must not happen: 'a saved BF16/no offload/auto-load for a small model must not load a large one so.' The menu then prints 'The same start without the menu: ... --model black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-Krea-dev --quant none --offload none'. That command would not auto-load, because an explicit --model that differs from the saved one sets the saved settings aside. The picker's overrides sentence then says '...when --menu names another checkpoint, its saved loading options are set aside too', which is false for the startup load.
findings.repro: 1. Save Anima / BF16 / No offload / Load automatically on startup from the picker (or write local-diffusion.settings.json by hand). 2. Run `uv run python -m backend.main --menu`, press Enter, choose FLUX.1 Krea [dev], press Enter. 3. The server starts loading FLUX Krea dev in BF16 with no offload immediately, on a 16 GB card.
findings.evidence: Scratch driver menu_test.py called launch.configure with ask answers ['', '1', '']. The printed environment is quoted above. apply_saved_environment(model=args.model) runs with model=None before the menu, so the saved model never meets the menu's choice.
findings.finder_recommendation: When --menu picks a model other than the saved one, drop the saved PRELOAD as an explicit --model does. Simplest is to run the menu first and then call apply_saved_environment(model=choice.model_id). Alternatively, add a load-on-startup question to the menu and record load_on_startup as '--menu' in the overrides, so the menu, its printed command and the page sentence all agree.
findings.verifier_reason: Reproduced in-process with a scratch driver (scratchpad/verify-model-switching/menu_test.py). It saves Anima/none/none/load_on_startup=true to a scratch settings file and calls launch.configure(['--menu']) with the answers ['', '1', '']. The resulting environment was MODEL_ID=black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-Krea-dev, QUANT=none, OFFLOAD=none, PRELOAD=true, STARTUP_OVERRIDES={model_id,quantization,offload:'--menu'}. The menu's printed equivalent was '--model black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-Krea-dev --quant none --offload none', which drops the saved preload. Cause: launch.py:270 calls apply_saved_environment(model=args.model) with args.model=None before the menu runs (launch.py:277-280). The menu's defaults are themselves the other checkpoint's saved BF16/no offload. rules.md:440-445 and design-notes:1697-1704 say an explicit model other than the saved one sets all four aside. The menu breaks that rule, and the page sentence at model-switch.js:499 then misstates it. This is the same ~25 GB unoffloaded auto-load that the design notes record as the reason for the rule. The --menu is an opt-in legacy path, so medium stands.
findings.verifier_recommendation: In configure(), when args.menu is set, run the menu before apply_saved_environment and pass model=choice.model_id, or re-run the 'model differs from saved' check after the menu and drop the saved PRELOAD/QUANT/OFFLOAD when it differs. Record load_on_startup in the overrides when it is dropped. Add a test in tests/test_launch*.py with saved Anima+preload, a menu pick of Krea dev, and an assertion that PRELOAD is not 'true'.

findings.title: During Switch & load's whole load (possibly a multi-minute first download), Generate, Check, tag lookup and LoRAs answer 409; Apply & save then Load reaches the same state with all of them working
findings.location: backend/main.py:630-670 (_switch_model holds _switching through ensure_loaded); backend/main.py:346-350 (middleware 409 while _switching); web/generation.js:233-240, web/model-switch.js:409-411
findings.observed: I set /api/fake/load to 6 s and posted /api/model/switch {model_id: Kohaku, load: true}. While it loaded: POST /api/prompt/analyze returned 409 'the checkpoint is switching; wait for the switch to finish', and GET /api/tags/suggest, GET /api/loras and POST /api/generate returned the same 409. After unload and a plain POST /api/model/load (state loading, switching false), /api/prompt/analyze and /api/tags/suggest returned 200 and /api/generate was accepted and queued (200 with a job_id). In the page during the switch's load, Generate was aria-disabled with the title 'Wait for the model settings change to finish', and Unload was held the same way. The selection is already committed at select(), and _refuse_busy_switch already refuses a second switch while the load lock is held, so keeping the reservation through ensure_loaded only blocks cold work. The rules say Check 'works cold' and is never blocked by a load. The design notes do not give a reason for holding the reservation through the load.
findings.repro: 1. POST /api/fake/load {"seconds":8}. 2. In Models, choose another row and press Switch & load. 3. Close the picker and press Check, Tags or Generate during the load. Every one is refused. 4. Compare with Apply & save followed by the topbar's Load: all of them work and Generate queues behind the load.
findings.evidence: curl session on port 7920: four 409 bodies during the switch, then 200s and a queued job during the plain load (outputs above). Page: els.generate.title read 'Wait for the model settings change to finish' while modelState was 'loading'.
findings.finder_recommendation: End the exclusive _switching reservation once select() has published the new snapshot, and let the load continue as an ordinary ensure_loaded that requests queue behind, as they do after Load. The load lock already keeps a second switch out. If keeping the reservation is deliberate, say so in rules.md, and have the note say that Check and Generate are held until the load ends.
findings.verifier_reason: Reproduced the asymmetry on fake port 8020 with fake load set to 6 s. During Switch & load, POST /api/prompt/analyze and GET /api/loras answered 409 'the checkpoint is switching; wait for the switch to finish' and status showed switching:true. After unload, a plain POST /api/model/load gave analyze 200 and loras 200 with state loading and switching false. The behaviour is deliberate and documented, though. CLAUDE.md says 'Switching reserves the idle server through cleanup and ensure_loaded', and rules.md:404-407 says the server 'holds it through ... unload, selection and ensure_loaded'. The code matches: main.py:658 clears _switching only in finally, after await ensure_loaded(). So this is a documented design choice with a real UX cost, not a bug. The finder's claim that it is undocumented is wrong; only the rationale is missing. Workaround: Apply & save then Load. Downgraded to low.
findings.verifier_recommendation: Treat it as a design change, not a fix. After select() and setting _load_state='loading' under the lock, clear _switching before awaiting ensure_loaded. _refuse_busy_switch already refuses a second switch while state=='loading' or the lock is held. Keep switch_error only for failures before select(). Update the CLAUDE.md and rules.md wording together, and add an API test showing analyze returning 200 during a switch's load. If the hold is kept, give its reason in design-notes, and make the Models note say that Check, tags and Generate wait until the load ends.

findings.title: Pausing a grid with a time budget uses up the budget while it is paused, so Resume can end the job at once with 'Time budget reached'.
findings.location: backend/jobs.py:296 (deadline set once at submit), 550-555 (checked before each cell), 602-628 (_hold never moves the deadline)
findings.observed: I ran a grid of 8 seeds with budget_minutes 0.25 and paused it after cell 2 (about 4 s in). It stayed paused for 20 s and then I pressed Resume. The job ended straight away with no new cell: 'Time budget reached after 2/8 cells — kept 2 images. Resume finishes the rest.' The tab title said 'Time budget reached'. While it was paused, the cell line said only 'Paused after cell 2/8 · GPU handed back' and never warned that the budget was still running.
findings.repro: Fake server with --step 0.3. In the page: startJob('/api/grid', {...collect(), prompt:'budget grid', steps:6, seeds:8, seed:5, budget_minutes:0.25}). When the progress reads 'cell 2/8', press Pause. Wait 20 s, then press Resume.
findings.evidence: scratchpad/jobs-multitab/s6.mjs output. After resume: {busy:false, err:'Time budget reached after 2/8 cells — kept 2 images. Resume finishes the rest.', title:'Time budget reached — Local Diffusion'}. Job.deadline is absolute (time.time() + budget at submit) and _hold only polls pause_requested. docs/design-notes.md 'Time budget' covers the load and the queue counting against the budget, but says nothing about a pause.
findings.finder_recommendation: In _hold, move job.deadline forward by the time spent paused (record time.monotonic() at entry and add the difference on resume). Pause exists to lend out the card, not to spend the night's budget. If the current behaviour is meant, the paused cell line and Pause's title should say the budget keeps running and show how much is left. Add a test in tests/test_jobs*.py: pause past the deadline, resume, and assert the next cell runs.
findings.verifier_reason: Reproduced over the API on my own fake server (port 8025, --step 0.3, scratch --data). I posted /api/grid with seeds 8, steps 6 and budget_minutes 0.25, paused when run reached 3, which was acknowledged at 5.5 s with 3 images, waited 18 s, then resumed. Final state: status 'cancelled', stopped_by 'budget', run 3/8, 3 images, at 23.7 s. Resume ran no new cell. In the code, backend/jobs.py:495 sets the absolute deadline at submit, _hold (jobs.py:801-829) only polls pause_requested, and the deadline check at jobs.py:749 comes right after the hold. design-notes 'Time budget' (3298) and the budget-preview section (2361) say only that the budget runs from submission and counts the load and the queue. Neither mentions a pause, and no earlier review covers it.
findings.verifier_recommendation: In _hold, record time.monotonic() on entry and on exit add the paused span to job.deadline when it is not None. The jobs.py:749 check then measures working time only, and the server-side 'left (budget)' estimate (deadline - started_at - elapsed) moves with it. Add a test that pauses past the deadline, resumes, and asserts the next cell runs. Also note in the Time budget section of design-notes that a pause stops the budget's clock.

findings.title: A plain Generate whose every image failed ends with the tab title '✓ Finished 0 images', and the messages use the grid word 'cells' for a plain job.

findings.title: Pause pressed on a job that is still queued says it will pause 'after this image', then holds the job before its first image while it keeps the GPU queue; the backend docstring says a pause means nothing for a queued job.
findings.location: backend/jobs.py:336-348 (pause docstring), 544-545 (_generate holds at index 0); web/job-progress.js:181-182, 266-276 (showCell/syncPause)
findings.observed: Tab B's single-image job is queued behind A's paused job. In B, Pause is enabled (aria-disabled false). Pressing it shows 'Pausing…' and the cell line 'pausing after this image… · The job ahead is paused…', although nothing of B's is running. The server keeps pause_requested=true on the queued job. Once A finished, B's job started and held at once: 'Paused before the first image · GPU handed back'. It kept the gate, so anything queued behind it waits too. JobManager.pause's docstring says 'A running job is the only kind this means anything for; a queued one holds its place either way'. The code instead latches the request.
findings.repro: Fake server with --step 0.3, two tabs. In A, run Repeat 8 and press Pause after image 1. In B, Generate one image (it queues), then press Pause in B. Resume A and let it finish. B's job is now paused before its first image.
findings.evidence: scratchpad/jobs-multitab/s4.mjs output: server jobs [['pause A','running',true,true,null],['queued B','queued',true,false,'paused']]. Later: B {pause:'Resume', cell:'Paused before the first image · GPU handed back'}.
findings.finder_recommendation: Decide which behaviour is intended. If the latch is meant ('hold my job when its turn comes'), word it for a queued job: the button's title and the cell line should say 'will hold before its first image', and the docstring should be fixed. If it is not meant, hold Pause with aria-disabled and a reason while the job is queued, and have pause() refuse a queued job.
findings.verifier_reason: The behaviour is deliberate. design-notes 'Pause' says 'A running job of one cell has no boundary to stop at (a queued one does: _generate checks before cell 0)', so latching a pause on a queued job, which then holds before its first image, is the documented design, and rules.md:941 holds Pause only for a running one-cell job. Two parts are real. The JobManager.pause docstring (jobs.py:540-541: 'A running job is the only kind this means anything for; a queued one holds its place either way') contradicts both the code and design-notes. And the cell line for a queued job reads 'pausing after this image…' (job-progress.js:161-162), though nothing has run yet. Holding the gate behind your own requested pause is what a pause does, so it is not a defect.
findings.verifier_recommendation: Fix the docstring to say a pause on a queued job holds it before its first cell. In showCell and syncPause, when job.status === 'queued' (run 0), say 'will hold before its first image' and title Pause 'Hold this job before it starts; Resume lets it run'. Do not refuse the pause on a queued job.

findings.verifier_reason: Not present. grep finds no paused_at, paused_since or pausedAt in backend/ or web/. The paused branch of showCell (job-progress.js:151-160) and WAITING.paused (job-stream.js:34-36) give no duration. It is feasible because no GPU is involved: one float on Job, set in _hold. Its link to finding 0 is weaker once that is fixed, since the pause would no longer spend the budget.

findings.title: A typed seed above 2^53 is silently changed to a different seed before it is sent
findings.observed: On FLUX.1 Krea I typed 9007199254740993 into Seed and pressed Generate. collect() sent 9007199254740992, and the record, the finish line ('Finished 1 image in 0s, seed 9007199254740992') and Use seed all carry …992, while the box still shows …993. Nothing warns. The schema accepts seeds up to 2^63-1, and when 99999999999999999999 was typed the server's refusal said so: 'seed: Input should be less than or equal to 9223372036854775807'. That invites seeds the page cannot send exactly. design-notes 'Seeds fit in a double' says 'a hand-entered 2**60 is still itself'. That holds from the CLI, but from the browser it holds only for the few values a double represents exactly (2**60 happens to be one of them).
findings.repro:
1. Any fake server.
2. Seed = 9007199254740993, prompt 'a fox'.
3. Generate.
4. Read the finish line and viewerRecords[0].seed.
findings.evidence: Browser log: collect().seed → 9007199254740992 with box '9007199254740993'; finish 'Finished 1 image in 0s, seed 9007199254740992.' Seeds pasted from other tools (for example ComfyUI's 64-bit draws) are usually above 2^53.
findings.finder_recommendation: Refuse in the page any Seed that is not Number.isSafeInteger, with a sentence such as 'Seeds above 9007199254740991 cannot be sent exactly from the browser; use the CLI or a smaller seed'. Alternatively, send the seed as a string the schema coerces. Give the input max=9007199254740991 so the browser marks it invalid too.
findings.verifier_reason: Reproduced the cause. In node, +'9007199254740993' gives 9007199254740992 and Number.isSafeInteger is false. web/generation.js:8,37 sends `+seed`, and #seed (index.html:423) has min=0 and no max. A curl POST /api/generate with seed 9007199254740993 came back exactly 9007199254740993, so only the page rounds. Downgraded: the record, the finish line and Use seed all carry the seed that actually ran, so no metadata is wrong and the gallery reproduces. The only mismatch is the box against the seed used. Seeds pasted from other tools (ComfyUI) would not reproduce their image in these pipelines anyway. design-notes 'Seeds fit in a double' covers drawn seeds and the CLI, not typed ones.
findings.verifier_recommendation: In collect(), or in generate() and startJob, refuse a Seed that is not Number.isSafeInteger, for example: 'Seeds above 9007199254740991 cannot be sent exactly from the browser; use a smaller seed or the CLI.' findings.title: `generate.py` loses the render and stops the whole night if the gallery is held by another process for more than SESSION_WAIT at save time; the server's job worker retries in this case
findings.location: backend/generate.py:1047-1065 (save_image in the cell loop), 1066-1069 (outer except); compare backend/jobs.py:849-870
findings.observed: In the CLI loop `p.storage.save_image(...)` sits outside the per-cell try. A `gallery_lock.GalleryBusy` (another process held the reservation past SESSION_WAIT = 30 s, e.g. a browser bundle export or a CLI reindex) reaches the outer `except Exception`. That prints the error and returns 1, discarding the denoised images in memory and every remaining cell. jobs.py retries in a loop for exactly this ('The render is in memory: wait again rather than lose it'). The `--resume` lookup at generate.py:703 has no handler either, so the same busy gallery gives a raw traceback there.
findings.repro: Copy of tests/test_cli.py's `cli` fixture with gallery_lock.SESSION_WAIT patched to 0.3 s. After the first cell's generate(), another thread takes `gallery_lock.hold(db_path)` (stands in for an export). Run `generate.main(['a fox','--seed','7','--runs','3','--width','256','--height','256'])`.
findings.evidence: Probe (scratch backend-correctness/copy2/tests/test_probe_busy.py): rc 1, stderr "GalleryBusy: another Local Diffusion process is using the gallery; try again when it finishes", 0 rows saved out of 3 cells. The equivalent server path keeps waiting (jobs.py while-True with GalleryBusy, ending only on cancel).
findings.finder_recommendation: Wrap the CLI save in the same retry as jobs.py: loop on GalleryBusy, log once per wait, stop on `stop` (Ctrl-C). Catch GalleryBusy around the resume lookup and print one line. Add a test_cli case like the probe.
findings.verifier_reason: Reproduced with my own probe (test_probes.py::test_cli_busy, using tests/test_cli.py's `cli` fixture). `gallery_lock.SESSION_WAIT` was patched to 0.3 s. After the fake backend's first generate(), another thread takes `gallery_lock.hold(db_path)`. `generate.main(['a fox','--seed','7','--runs','3','--width','256','--height','256'])` returned 1 after a single generate call. stderr: 'GalleryBusy: another Local Diffusion process is using the gallery; try again when it finishes'. 0 rows saved. generate.py:1047 `p.storage.save_image(...)` sits outside the per-cell try, so the error reaches the outer `except Exception` (1066-1069). rules.md:1226 and design-notes ~3543 require the job path never to drop a finished render (`jobs._save` retries until cancel, jobs.py:849-870), and the CLI has no such retry. One mitigation: cells saved earlier stay, and `--resume` re-runs the rest. So the loss is the render in hand plus the rest of an unattended run, not the whole night's output. The resume lookup at generate.py:703 is also unguarded, which I confirmed by reading only; I did not run it.
findings.verifier_recommendation: Wrap the CLI save in a loop like `jobs._save`: on `gallery_lock.GalleryBusy`, print one stderr line ('gallery busy in another process; still waiting to save') and retry. Let KeyboardInterrupt still end it, since the SIGINT handler or `stop` flag decides. Around `completed_cells` for --resume, catch GalleryBusy and print one line with exit code 1 instead of a traceback. Add a test_cli case shaped like the probe that asserts all 3 rows land once the holder releases.

findings.title: An older-schema database restored over the same path while the process runs is never migrated, so every gallery read fails until restart, although the code comments and a test comment say this case is handled
findings.observed: `_migrated` is keyed only on `str(settings.db_path)`. `_connect` clears it only when the path changes, and the per-connection CREATE TABLE runs only when the table is missing. A backup from before `batch`/`binned_at` copied over local-diffusion.db therefore skips `_migrate`. The comment at line 182 says 'a restored older file needs its columns again'. test_a_database_from_before_job_ids_gains_the_column says 'a file swapped under a running server - restored from a backup - has to be checked again regardless', but it uses a different path (old.db), so it only tests the path-change reset.
findings.repro: In one process: init_db() on a fresh gallery (migration recorded for that path). Delete the db and its -wal/-shm, create an images table without batch and binned_at at the same path, then call storage.list_images() and storage.get_image(1, include_binned=True).
findings.evidence: Probe (scratch backend-correctness/probe_migrate.py): list_images -> "OperationalError no such column: binned_at"; get_image -> "IndexError No item with that key" (from _row_to_record reading row['batch']/['binned_at']). Restarting the process fixes it. bundles.py:172 resets `storage._migrated = None` for its own replacement, which shows the gap is known for that one path.
findings.finder_recommendation: Key the check on the file's identity as well as its path (st_ino/st_ctime_ns, or PRAGMA schema_version), or run the cheap PRAGMA table_info comparison on every _connect. Change the test to replace the file at the same path after one migration has run.
findings.verifier_reason: Reproduced (test_probes.py::test_restore_same_path). After init_db and one save, I deleted the db and its -wal/-shm, wrote an `images` table without the newer columns at the same path, and called `storage.list_images()`. It raised `sqlite3.OperationalError: no such column: binned_at` (storage.py:717). `_connect` resets `_migrated` only when the path changes (storage.py:260-262), and `_migrate` returns early on a matching path (199-201). Adjusted because this is not a new gap: it is an incomplete fix of docs/review-2026-09-07.md:1269 ('storage.py:70 _migrated flag defeats per-connection recovery', closed in 8f947a9 by keying on the path, per review-2026-09-07-checklist.md:117). That finding named 'restore last week's db over a running server', the same-path case the fix does not cover. The comment at storage.py:182-186 still claims it is handled. With binned_at in every live read, the effect is now wider than the original save failure: the gallery reads fail too, and a job's save_image fails with OperationalError, so the render is lost. Low severity stays because the trigger is restoring a file under a running server.
findings.verifier_recommendation: Do what the 2026-09-07 review first proposed: drop the cache and run `PRAGMA table_info(images)` in `_migrate` on every `_connect`, which costs about the same as the sqlite_master lookup beside it. Alternatively, key `_migrated` on (path, PRAGMA schema_version) or on the file's st_ino/st_mtime_ns. Then remove the `storage._migrated = None` special case in bundles.py:172. Rewrite test_a_database_from_before_job_ids_gains_the_column to replace the file at the same path after a migration has already run in-process.

findings.title: Two rules have no test that fails when they are broken: no_grad instead of inference_mode around the pipeline call, and resetting the LoRA record when a re-weighting fails
findings.observed: Mutation 1: `with torch.no_grad(), ...` changed to `with torch.inference_mode(), ...`. The full suite still passed (2594 passed, 6 skipped), and no test mentions inference_mode. Mutation 2: `self._lora = None` removed from the except branch of `_apply_lora`. Still green. The only failure test fails the first `load_lora_weights`, where `_lora` is already None. The case the reset protects is a scale change on an attached adapter whose `set_adapters` raises. Without the reset the next cell asking for the old weight sees `wanted == self._lora`, skips the reload and renders with no adapter under a row that records one.
findings.repro: Copy the repo to scratch with git archive and apply each one-line mutation. Run `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest -q tests` from the copy.
findings.evidence: scratch backend-correctness/mut_full.log: "[inference_mode] rc=0 2594 passed", "[lora not cleaned on fail] rc=0 2594 passed". The other 15 mutations failed tests, e.g. test_one_generator_per_image_seeded_seed_plus_i, test_a_scheduler_that_does_not_shift_dynamically_still_lands_on_mu[3.0], test_a_committed_image_survives_a_rename_that_keeps_failing.
findings.finder_recommendation: (a) In test_schedule, give a fake pipeline a `__call__` that asserts `torch.is_grad_enabled() is False and not torch.is_inference_mode_enabled()`, and run it through DiffusersBackend.generate. (b) In test_conditioning, use SwapPipeline with set_adapters raising on the second call: apply (A, 0.5), then (A, 0.8) and expect a raise, then (A, 0.5) and assert load_lora_weights was called again (or `_lora is None` after the raise).
findings.verifier_reason: Re-ran both mutations myself on fresh `git archive HEAD` copies under scratch (verify-backend-correctness/ma, mb), and checked that the mutant's own backend module was the one imported. (a) `with torch.no_grad(), schedule.forced_mu` changed to `torch.inference_mode()` at diffusers_backend.py:729: full suite 2594 passed, 6 skipped. (b) `self._lora = None` removed from `_apply_lora`'s except branch (line 530): 2594 passed, 6 skipped. grep finds no test mentioning inference_mode or is_grad_enabled. test_a_failed_injection_leaves_no_half_applied_adapter (test_conditioning.py:267) fails the first load, where `_lora` is already None, so the reset is never exercised. The case it guards is real. From (A,0.5), a request for (A,0.8) where set_adapters raises unloads the adapter but leaves `_lora=(A,0.5)`. A later (A,0.5) cell then hits `wanted == self._lora`, returns early, and renders with no adapter under a row that records one. The code is correct today, so only the test is missing.
findings.verifier_recommendation: (a) In test_schedule or test_conditioning, give a fake pipeline a `__call__` that records `torch.is_grad_enabled()` and `torch.is_inference_mode_enabled()`, run it through `DiffusersBackend.generate`, and assert (False, False). Do the same for the refine path (`_refine`). (b) Give SwapPipeline a `fail_set_on` counter. Apply (style, 0.5), then (style, 0.8) and expect a raise, then (style, 0.5) and assert `len(pipe.loaded) == 2` and `backend._lora == ('style.safetensors', 0.5)`.

findings.title: The only way to export images is to bundle the whole gallery and clear it: there is no backup that keeps the gallery, and no export of starred or picked images
findings.observed: The Bundles dialog offers 'Refresh counts | Bundle & clear gallery | Import selected file | Cancel upload' and nothing else. Sharing ten starred images, or taking a routine backup, therefore means clearing the gallery, or copying files like 20261012-102601-13-ef9e18.png out of outputs/ by hand. Done by hand, that loses stars and timings, as design-notes 'Gallery bundles' itself says.
findings.repro: Fake server with a fresh --data; generate 3 images; open Bundles…. The only export is 'Type 3 to confirm all gallery records will be removed' followed by 'Bundle & clear gallery'.
findings.evidence: Screenshot d-bundles.png at 2560x1305. The dialog intro says 'Save all images… then clear the gallery'. The listed buttons came from a DOM query.
findings.finder_recommendation: Add two options. (a) 'Back up (keep gallery)': the same verified archive (bundle_archive + bundle_crypto), skipping the cleanup step. (b) 'Export picked/filter': a bundle or plain ZIP of the selection or filter, with PNGs only (their local-diffusion and A1111 chunks already carry the settings) or with a sub-database so they can be imported again. Reuse resolve_selection and the gallery reservation. Risks: free disk space for a full copy, and a partial bundle whose refine or reference links point outside it (import already reports unrecoverable links).
findings.verifier_reason: Reproduced on my own fake server (port 8050, FLUX.1-Krea-dev, fresh --data). The Bundles dialog shows only Close, Refresh counts, Bundle & clear gallery, Import selected file and Cancel upload. Its intro reads 'Save all images... then clear the gallery'. In the code, ExportRequest is only {expected, password} (api_bundles.py:28-30), and POST /export always runs bundles.export_bundle (api_bundles.py:203-208), which removes the sources (bundles.py:354). Design-notes 'Gallery bundles' (3429ff) explains the verify-before-clear order. It gives no reason why a backup that keeps the gallery should be left out, and no earlier review proposes one. findings.verifier_recommendation: Add a keep_gallery flag to ExportRequest, threaded into export_bundle. It skips only the second-inventory and cleanup block and keeps the verified read-back. Show it as a 'Back up (keep gallery)' button that needs no typed count. Do this first, at about effort S. Exporting the selection or the filter is a second step (M). Build its sub-database through resolve_selection, and have the import's existing link checks report refine or reference sources that the bundle does not contain. Hold the gallery reservation for both steps. Before a full copy, check free disk space against the inventory size.

That route reuses generate.py's _image_settings and embedded_metadata, moved into a shared module, and returns a GenerateRequest-shaped object that has gone through applied(). findings.title: No inpainting or regional edit, although diffusers 0.40 ships inpaint siblings for the catalogue's FLUX.1, SDXL, Z-Image, Qwen-Image and FLUX.2 [klein] pipelines over the same components

Each __call__ takes image, mask_image, strength, generator and callback_on_step_end, so each meets load()'s rule. findings.evidence: Output: FluxInpaintPipeline ['image','mask_image','strength','padding_mask_crop','generator','callback_on_step_end','masked_image_latents']; the same for the SDXL, Qwen, Z-Image and Flux2Klein classes.
findings.finder_recommendation: Generalise refine.sibling to a suffix ('Img2Img' or 'Inpaint') under the same exact-export and REQUIRED checks. Add a GenerateRequest.mask: the mask stored as a gallery-side PNG keyed by a hash, carried in applied(), a new column with a _migrate entry, and the PNG chunk. Add a brush and eraser canvas in the lightbox or Refine dialog, and outpaint later as inpaint over a padded canvas. Risks: none of the authors' guides document base-model inpainting (BFL ships a separate FLUX.1 Fill), so the guide text has to say it is unsourced (heuristic) and must not invent advice. The mask also has to enter the reproduction set and bundles.
findings.verifier_reason: In the venv I ran inspect.signature on the __call__ of FluxInpaintPipeline, StableDiffusionXLInpaintPipeline, ZImageInpaintPipeline, QwenImageInpaintPipeline, Flux2KleinInpaintPipeline and FluxFillPipeline. All six exist in diffusers 0.40 and take image, mask_image, strength, generator and callback_on_step_end. A grep for mask_image or inpaint in backend/ and web/ finds nothing. refine.sibling (refine.py:74-101) hard-codes the 'Img2Img' suffix, so generalising it is feasible. findings.verifier_recommendation: Scope it in phases. (1) Backend: give sibling(pipeline, kind) the 'Img2Img' or 'Inpaint' suffix under the same exact-export and REQUIRED/CARRIED checks. Store the mask as a gallery-side PNG named by its hash, add a GenerateRequest.mask_hash that is part of applied(), a column with a _migrate entry, the PNG chunk, and bundle inventory entries. (2) UI: a brush and eraser canvas in the Refine dialog (not a panel mode, per design-notes 'A dialog, not a mode of the panel'). The guides should label base-model inpainting as heuristic, since no author documents it; FluxFill is a separate 23 GB checkpoint and stays out of scope. Outpainting can come later. The highest risk is keeping the reproduction set and bundles complete once a mask file is part of them.

findings.title: A reference image moved to the recycle bin in another tab is refused at every Generate with the server's 'reference image N' wording, where N is the gallery id and not the chip number, and the chip is never dropped

findings.observed: On klein, references were [3,4] (chips image 1 and image 2), then #4 was binned through POST /api/images/bin. Ctrl+Enter returned the error 'reference image 4 is in the recycle bin; restore it to use it'. referenceIds stayed [3,4], no chip was marked .gone and the card for #4 was still shown. A second Ctrl+Enter gave the same refusal and nothing was queued (newest id still 6). In the first run the references were [6,4,5]: the gallery's #4 was chip 'image 2', but the message said 'reference image 4'. With four chips, that wording points at the wrong chip. The page's binned branch in dropRefusedReferences ('been moved to the recycle bin') cannot be reached from a submit, because the server's binned refusal never matches its regex. The Refine dialog has the same gap: with #5 binned while its dialog was open, Refine showed 'source image 5 is in the recycle bin; restore it to use it' twice. It never used the page's own sentence ('#5 is in the recycle bin; restore it to refine it.', as bin.js words it) and never marked the source line.
findings.repro:
1. Start fake_server --model black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-klein-4B with a fresh --data, then generate 4 images.
2. Click ❐ on cards #3 and #4 and type a prompt.
3. From another tab (or curl), POST /api/images/bin {"ids":[4]}.
4. Press Generate twice.
5. For the Refine variant, on a FLUX.1 fake open ⤢ on a card, bin that image through the API, then press Refine twice.
findings.evidence:
Run 1: {refs:[6,4,5], err:'reference image 4 is in the recycle bin; restore it to use it', chips:['Reference image 1 (gallery #6)','Reference image 2 (gallery #4)',...]}.
Run 2: n:1 and n:2 both gave {refs:[3,4], err:'reference image 4 is in the recycle bin; restore it to use it', chipGone:0}, newest id 6.
Refine: {open:true, err:'source image 5 is in the recycle bin; restore it to use it'} twice.
The rule in docs/rules.md:782-797 covers only the 'no gallery image with id N' refusal.
findings.finder_recommendation: Have the server word the binned case so the page can match it, or extend dropRefusedReferences to the '<noun> N is in the recycle bin' form and route it through dropGoneReferences, which already reports binned. That marks or drops the chip and says 'reference #4 has been moved to the recycle bin…' in the page's #N wording. Do the same in refineSourceGone ('#5 is in the recycle bin…', source line marked). Add a binned case to smoke-conditioning and smoke-refine.

findings.title: An adapter file removed or renamed while the page is open stays selectable, and Generate or Refine shows the server's developer message (full path and env var) at every press, with the Refine dialog having no way to drop the carried LoRA
findings.location: web/status.js:757-806 (refreshLoras runs only on the first status and at load); web/generation.js:32-33; web/refine.js:289-298, 682-683 (refineLora fixed, no control); backend/loras.py:60-68
findings.checkpoints: any checkpoint with lora_supported (checked on FLUX.1 Krea dev)
findings.observed: In the panel on the FLUX.1 fake, I picked demo-style.safetensors at weight 0.6, renamed the file, then pressed Generate twice. #error showed: no LoRA named 'demo-style.safetensors' in C:\...\data-flux\loras; put a .safetensors adapter there (LOCAL_DIFFUSION_LORAS_DIR moves the directory). The select still offered and held demo-style.safetensors, and the renamed file was not listed. The second press gave the same refusal. Nothing re-asks /api/loras, unlike references, where a refusal drops the gone chip (A78). In the Refine dialog on #3 (made with demo-style at 0.7), the line read 'LoRA demo-style.safetensors at 0.7, as #3 was made.'. After the rename, Refine showed the same raw message in #refine-error and the dialog stayed open. refineLora has no control, so the pass cannot run without the adapter or at another weight until the page is reloaded. On the good side, the record is never written without its LoRA: the server refuses rather than drops.
findings.repro:
1. Start fake_server --model black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-Krea-dev --data <scratch>; it plants loras/demo-style.safetensors.
2. Load the page, pick demo-style, set weight 0.6 and type a prompt.
3. Rename <scratch>/loras/demo-style.safetensors.
4. Press Generate twice.
5. For the dialog: with the file present, open ⤢ on a record made with that LoRA, rename the file, then press Refine.
findings.evidence:
Panel, presses 1 and 2: {err:"no LoRA named 'demo-style.safetensors' in C:\\...\\data-flux\\loras; put a .safetensors adapter there (LOCAL_DIFFUSION_LORAS_DIR moves the directory)", lora:'demo-style.safetensors', opts:['','demo-style.safetensors']}.
Dialog: {open:true, err:<same message>, carried:'LoRA demo-style.safetensors at 0.7, as #3 was made.'}.
HTTP: POST /api/generate with that lora returned 422 with the same detail.
findings.finder_recommendation: On a 422 that names the chosen adapter (or `lora_missing`), call refreshLoras() and say it in the page's words, for example 'demo-style.safetensors is no longer in the LoRA folder, so it was taken out of LoRA. Generate again to run without it.', as dropRefusedReferences does. In the Refine dialog, re-read the list on that refusal and switch refineCarried to its 'not applied' wording. Optionally give the dialog a small 'without the LoRA' toggle so a pass can run without the adapter on purpose. Refreshing /api/loras when the select is focused would also pick up files dropped in, which today needs a reload.

findings.title: Ctrl-C while a job waits on the load does not end that job: shutdown hangs for the 30 s graceful timeout (or until the load ends), uvicorn logs an ASGI traceback, and the tab never hears 'Server stopped'
findings.location: backend/jobs.py:410-416 (stop_all), backend/jobs.py:583-603 (_run awaiting ensure_loaded), backend/main.py:849-852 (Server.handle_exit), backend/main.py:866 (timeout_graceful_shutdown=30)
findings.observed: stop_all('shutdown') only sets cancel_requested and stopped_by. A job still in _run awaiting self._ensure_loaded() is never finished, unlike jobs.cancel(), which calls _finish at once for a queued job. Its SSE stream therefore stays open. uvicorn drains connections before the lifespan runs, so shutdown waits for the load. With a 20 s load, done(cancelled, stopped_by=shutdown) arrived only when the load ended (log: 'model ready' then 'job … cancelled: 0 image(s) in 20s'), 17 s after the signal. With a 45-60 s load (a real first load takes minutes), uvicorn logged 'ERROR: Cancel 1 running task(s), timeout graceful shutdown exceeded' and 'ERROR: Exception in ASGI application' (CancelledError traceback) after 30 s. The stream was cut without a done event (curl rc=18) and the job never reached _finish. In the browser, for ~30 s after the signal the owning tab kept 'loading weights · 0:33' with the clock ticking and the indeterminate bar, while the topbar said 'server not answering — retrying'. After the server came back it said 'The server restarted, and this job ended with it before any of it had finished.' (title 'Lost the job'). A running job stopped the same way says 'Stopped: the server is shutting down — nothing had finished.' (title 'Server stopped').
findings.repro: 1) Start a server through main.Server (as main.run does), e.g. the scratch wrapper scratchpad/gap-load/fake_exit.py --port 7960 --model black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-Krea-dev --step 0.3 --data <fresh>. 2) POST /api/fake/load {seconds:60}; POST /api/model/unload. 3) In a tab press Generate (it shows 'loading weights'), or POST /api/generate and open GET /api/jobs/{id}/stream. 4) Send Ctrl-C (here server.handle_exit(SIGINT) via POST /api/scratch/exit). 5) Watch the server log and the tab for 40 s, then restart the server on the same --data.
findings.evidence: srv2.log/srv8a.log: 'Shutting down' / 'Waiting for connections to close. (CTRL+C to force quit)' / 'ERROR: Cancel 1 running task(s), timeout graceful shutdown exceeded' / 'ERROR: Exception in ASGI application … CancelledError: Task cancelled, timeout graceful shutdown exceeded'. sse2.txt has no '"type": "done"' line; curl exited 18. 20 s run: signal at t=377, done(status=cancelled, stopped_by=shutdown) and stream close at t=394, which is when the load ended. Browser at +15 s: progress 'loading weights · 0:18', status 'server not answering — retrying'. After restart: err 'The server restarted, and this job ended with it before any of it had finished.', title 'Lost the job — Local Diffusion'. Seen 4 times (2 curl, 2 browser). The only handle_exit test (tests/test_api_analysis_lifecycle.py:285) covers a running job only.
findings.finder_recommendation: In stop_all (or at least on the shutdown path), finish jobs still in status 'queued' through _finish(loop, job, 'cancelled'), as cancel() does, keeping stopped_by='shutdown'. Their streams then get done at once and the drain does not wait for the load; _run already returns quietly when _finish has run (done_sent guard). stop_all runs on the signal's thread, so do the _finish through loop.call_soon_threadsafe. Add a test: a job waiting on a slow load, handle_exit, assert done arrives with stopped_by 'shutdown' before the load ends.

findings.title: A held Unload press during a load leaves 'The weights are still loading.' in the panel line after the load finishes
findings.location: web/status.js:290-304 (unloadModel, the final else branch), web/status.js:711-714 (only unloadRefusal is cleared on ready)
findings.observed: While a load runs with no job (a preload at startup, or the Load button), Unload is aria-disabled with the title 'The weights are still loading'. Pressing it calls showError('The weights are still loading.', true), but does not record that text in unloadRefusal or elsewhereNote. The ready transition clears only unloadRefusal (the server's 409 text), so the sentence stays. 7 s after the topbar turned 'FLUX.1 Krea [dev]' and Unload was enabled again, the panel line still read 'The weights are still loading.' and was visible (height > 0). The job-held and other-tab-held presses are cleared when their reason ends. The 2026-10-04 review asked to 'Clear a leftover Unload 409 when the state turns ready'; that fix covers the server's refusal but not this local held-press path.
findings.repro: Fake server (FLUX.1-Krea-dev). POST /api/fake/load {seconds:6}; POST /api/model/unload; refresh. Click Load, then click Unload while 'loading…' shows. Wait for the topbar to read the bare model name and look at the panel's error line. Also reproduces by opening the page during a LOCAL_DIFFUSION_PRELOAD=true startup load and clicking Unload.
findings.evidence: s8 run at 1400x900 and at 2560x1305: 'press: err=The weights are still loading.' then '7s after ready: status=FLUX.1 Krea [dev] unload=false err="The weights are still loading." errVisible=true'. Screenshots: scratchpad/gap-load/stale-unload-7962.png and stale-unload-7962-wide.png. Also seen in the s7 run, where the line was still showing after the preload finished and another tab's job had started.
findings.finder_recommendation: In the final else branch of unloadModel, remember the said text (e.g. unloadRefusal = said) so the existing ready transition at status.js:711 clears it. Alternatively, clear any held-reason sentence when its hold lifts, as the job and elsewhere branches already do.

findings.title: In the default one-column layout, cards a finished job prepends shift every card along the rows under a resting pointer, so a card's no-confirm Move-to-bin control now acts on a different image
findings.location: web/job-results.js:464-466 (joinFinished waits only through galleryPointerGone); web/gallery.js:278-295 (galleryPointerGone resolves at once unless besideOn); web/gallery.js:264
findings.observed: With 1,600 images loaded deep (scrollY 6000, 5 cards a row at 1400x900), I measured the Move-to-bin button of #1476 at (941,394). Another tab's 1-image job then ended. At the same point the element became the button titled 'Move #1477 to the recycle bin'. With 3 images, the card under (900,500) went from #1456 to #1459. In both cases scrollY stayed 6000: scroll anchoring keeps the rows but not the slots. This page's own 2-image Generate moved the card under the pointer from #1459 to #1471 (scrollY 6000 to 5989). The same happened at 2560x1305 with Gallery beside off: the top-left visible card went from #1100 to #1104 after 4 images, scrollY 16237 unchanged. The code's own rationale for holding cards only in the beside column ('one image ahead of them moves every card a place along the rows, and a card about to be pressed was another by the press') applies just as much here. The comment at gallery.js:264 ('Back under the viewer, the page's own scroll anchoring has the gallery') does not hold for horizontal slot shifts. U25 (review-2026-10-04) saw the one-slot shift in its prototype but did not act on it.
findings.repro: 1. Start `uv run python tools/fake_server.py --port 7965 --model black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-Krea-dev --data <scratch>` on a gallery of a few hundred images. 2. At 1400x900, scroll down until about 300 cards are loaded and rest the pointer on a card's ⌦. 3. From another tab or curl, POST /api/generate {prompt:'x', width:256, height:256, num_images:1, steps:4}. 4. After the next 3 s status poll, the ⌦ under the pointer belongs to the neighbouring card. A click bins that card without confirmation. Reproduced 4 times (1, 3 and 4 images, and an own Generate) at both viewports.
findings.evidence: scale6 log: {aimed:'1476', under:'1477', title:'Move #1477 to the recycle bin'}. scale5: card 1456 became 1459, scrollY 6000 both times. scale4 at 2560: id 1100 became 1104, top 92 px both times. Code: galleryPointerGone() returns Promise.resolve() when !besideOn.
findings.finder_recommendation: Hold joinFinished's cards while the pointer rests on the window-scrolled grid too, with the same galleryPointer flag on #gallery's enter and leave (not :hover), released on leave. Or prepend only whole rows' worth while the pointer is in the grid. Add the one-column case to smoke-results or smoke-jobs.

findings.title: More seeds refuses to open when batches × the remembered count is over 1024, telling the user to 'Ask for fewer' while the count box is inside the dialog that never opens
findings.location: web/more-seeds.js:122-151 (opens only on a successful first preview); backend/api_more_seeds.py:57-64
findings.observed: With search 'fox' (320 single-image batches) and nothing selected, pressing More seeds… left the dialog closed. The gallery line said: '320 batches × 4 is 1280 images; a press may queue 1024. Ask for fewer, or pick fewer batches.' The same scope previews fine at count 3 (960) and count 1. With 1,024 cards Shift-picked, openMoreSeeds() gave '1015 batches × 4 is 4060 images…', also with no dialog. The opener's comment says a selection 'the server refuses whole (past a job's worth) is said in the gallery's line rather than in a dialog with nothing to queue'. That reason does not apply here, because a lower count would queue. The default count is 4 and the count remembers the last one queued, so any filter or selection over 256 batches is blocked. The only way out is to shrink the selection.
findings.repro: 1. On a gallery with more than 256 single-image batches matching a search, clear localStorage 'local-diffusion.more-seeds.v1'. 2. Type the search with no selection and press More seeds…. 3. The dialog does not open, and the line asks for fewer. 4. curl /api/more-seeds/preview with {search:'fox', favorites:false, count:3} answers 200 with 960 queued. Reproduced from the button (ms.json) and via openMoreSeeds() with 1,024 selected (scale7d).
findings.evidence: ms.json: [moreSeedsDialog.open=false, galleryError='320 batches × 4 is 1280 images; a press may queue 1024. Ask for fewer, or pick fewer batches.']. API: count 4 gives 422; count 3 gives 200 with ids listed.
findings.finder_recommendation: When the 422 is only the batches × count product, open the dialog anyway with the count clamped to floor(1024 / batches), at least 1, and say why. Or have the preview answer the batch count so the page can set the count before asking. Keep the gallery-line refusal for a selection whose batches alone are over the cap.

findings.title: Feature: let a running Expand be cancelled, above all a first use that downloads ERNIE's 7.4 GiB rewriter and holds the card
findings.location: web/prompt-expand.js (no cancel or abort path); backend/api_prompt.py:188-230 (run_when_idle(expand_prompt))
findings.observed: With the fake's Expand held and fresh, the line under the prompt read 'Downloading ERNIE's prompt rewriter (about 7.1 GiB) once, then expanding, then … translating… · 0:02'. No visible button anywhere on the page matched cancel or stop. Generate was aria-disabled with 'Wait for prompt expansion to finish', and Escape changed nothing. Generating stays blocked until the download, load and translation finish, which can take minutes. A14 in review-2026-10-05 noted 'no … cancel' and was fixed with the cost, clock and steps only.
findings.repro: 1. Start the fake on baidu/ERNIE-Image-Turbo. 2. POST /api/fake/expand {hold:true, fresh:true}. 3. Type a prompt and press Expand. 4. The page offers no way to stop it, and Generate stays held until POST /api/fake/expand {hold:false}.
findings.evidence: ernie.json log: cancel-like visible buttons = []; generate aria-disabled 'true', title 'Wait for prompt expansion to finish'; the prompt-note text quoted above.
findings.finder_recommendation: Add a Stop to the running line that aborts the page's request and frees the panel at once. On the server, mark the expansion abandoned so its result is dropped. Where it is still downloading, let the download finish into the cache in the background, or stop between the download, rewrite and translate steps, so the gate is released at the next step boundary.
